description.p: Sparkamp is an open-source, keyboard-driven audio player with a classic interface, built for Linux and GNOME. It supports MP3, OGG, FLAC and other common audio formats, and includes a full-featured 10-band equalizer, a media library, visualizer plugins, and custom CSS skinning.
Launch with sparkamp for the GTK4 graphical interface or sparkamp --tui for the terminal (TUI) mode.
A bug-fix release, focused on performance and drag-and-drop.

Every Media Library view can now be dragged onto the playlist. Five had no drag source at all: the album gallery, both disc views and both device views. Dragging a container adds everything in it, so an album brings its tracks, a saved playlist brings its tracks, a disc brings its tracks and a device brings its files.

The setting that decides whether adding files appends to the playlist or replaces it was previously ignored by drag-and-drop entirely, and applied inconsistently elsewhere. One rule now governs every route in, including the command line and files opened from the desktop. It is named "Default add file action" now, rather than for the one view it was first written for.

The album gallery opens about twice as quickly: clicking Albums used to rebuild the entire grid twice, the query that reads the library has moved into the database, the grid fills in a single operation rather than one per album, and returning to the gallery reuses what it already had. The album view is also searchable in the GTK and terminal frontends now, matching macOS.

Several drag-and-drop defects found on real hardware are fixed: dragging a CD track added a single entry named after the device node with no tags, a device row could not be dragged at all, an album could only be added once, and an external drop was discarded whenever playlist rows happened to be selected.

A stability release. No new headline feature: the work went into the two largest files in the tree and into the defects that came out from under them. A bulk folder ingest could pin the interface until the app had to be force-quit; the folder-watch drain is now bounded so it cannot starve the main loop. A folder reached through a symlink was indexed as a second copy of every track it held, growing thousands of duplicate rows; track paths are now canonicalized on the way in, and existing duplicates are merged on upgrade with their play counts intact.

The Media Library window reopens roughly nine times faster and no longer leaks on every close. The playlist editor can actually save playlists that live outside Sparkamp's own directory, Revert undoes a whole editing session rather than half of one, and unsaved changes are marked. Optical disc support improves across both frontends: data discs browse and import on macOS, discs no longer appear among sync devices, a disc that mounts as a whole device is readable, blocked burns explain themselves instead of dimming silently, and unreadable CD-TEXT is reported rather than shown as placeholder track names.

About thirty smaller fixes round it out, covering context-menu dispatch and placement, duration probing on every route into the playlist, Select All no longer freezing mouse selection, device sync moved off the interface thread, and consistent artwork rendering across all three library views.

Winamp parity reaches its full 12-phase roadmap. Now Playing grows an expandable panel and a standalone album art window (with inline media library thumbnails); playback integrates with the OS via Linux MPRIS2 and macOS Now Playing / remote commands; ReplayGain analyzes and normalizes volume across tracks and albums; a manual play queue lets you line up specific tracks ahead of shuffle or linear order; and a browse-by-cover album gallery joins the media library.

Playlists gain sort/randomize/reverse and a status row with count/duration/selection; watch folders auto-rescan and auto-add new music; disc CD-TEXT reading and source badges round out track metadata; and a right-click "View/Search Lyrics" opens a lyrics viewer (USLT tags, or a browser search fallback) from any track list, with toggle-to-close behavior. The Send-to menu and per-drive burn queues make copying tracks to playlists, devices, and disc burns a single consistent action across every view.

Every right-click context menu across GTK and macOS was re-aligned to the same order, labels, and actions, and a GTK popover sizing bug that made long menus scroll unnecessarily was fixed. A large settings cluster (play-stats thresholds, remembered per-view search, artist-fallback sorting) and a wide sweep of shortcut and dialog fixes round out the release.

Optical disc support across all three frontends: play audio CDs from the Media Library's new Disc Drives section, identify discs via gnudb.org and edit or submit corrected track lists, rip discs to tagged MP3s with per-track progress and automatic library import, and burn audio CDs or MP3 data discs (with a companion playlist) from a dedicated burn queue — including erase-with-confirmation for rewritable media, capacity meters, and cancellable burns. Sparkamp can also act as the system's audio-CD handler: inserting a disc opens the library at that drive (GNOME Removable Media / macOS CDs & DVDs settings; the in-app toggle is on by default).

Device sync grows richer file views, playlist management on the device, conflict resolution, and iOS/MTP recognition with honest capability messaging. The Granite visualizer gains a frame-rate-independent core, a Kaleidoscope fold fix with clean crossfades, an honest FPS/render readout naming the active effect, and steadier frame pacing on macOS. Failure handling hardened throughout: drive disconnects surface banners, scratched-disc rips retry then skip, burns report tool failures truthfully, and a watchdog kills wedged burner processes.

Granite becomes a built-in visualizer. The Geiss-inspired plasma now lives in the core (no separate plugin) with a warp-map feedback engine: 8 palettes, 12 warp effects, beat-reactive palette and effect rolling, and a flux beat detector that surfaces BPM and time signature. Press 'a' to cycle to Granite, 'e' for a random effect, 'f' or double-click for fullscreen; Settings exposes speed, palette, feedback, effect, and auto-switch, and credits the original by Ryan Geiss. The same renderer drives the GTK and macOS frontends under a single-driver rule so the mini and fullscreen views stay in sync, and the fullscreen 'g' overlay shows FPS, BPM, and meter.

Large internal refactor: the monolithic core and frontend files were split into focused modules (FFI, media library, shared tag/text/time helpers, and the TUI and macOS sources by domain) with no behavior change. Playlist handling now preserves a track's real, accessible path instead of substituting a stale catalogue row, so saved tracks no longer appear missing and unavailable files show the correct status; the ID3 editor gains an explicit "(undefined)" genre option and a selectable filename header.

Playlist editor overhaul. The specific-playlist view now uses a ColumnView mirroring the files-view columns (visibility, widths, order share the same config and refresh on every playlist load), gains a position column with canonical play-order tracking that survives duplicate entries, and an artwork View button to match the files view. Right-click menus across the active playlist, files view, and editor gain a unified Add to Playlist submenu with New Playlist… plus every saved playlist; Edit ID3 hides on multi-select; the editor's Remove now removes from the playlist (rewriting the M3U8) rather than the library DB. Multi-select drag-and-drop in the active playlist preserves the selection across GTK's transient collapse and reorders all dragged rows, with drop-position honoring before/after halves. Drag-reorder in the editor is gated to position-ASC sort. Several smaller fixes: BOM-prefixed M3U8 files parse correctly, default save directory falls back through first ML folder / ~/Music / home, save errors surface in a modal dialog, the artwork viewer reports decode failures inline, Delete key removes from the editor, the info-button glyph matches the surrounding mode-buttons, and a new crash log at ~/.config/sparkamp/crash.log captures panics + GLib criticals on Linux so silent crashes leave a trace.

First stable release. Adds macOS DMG build, GTK skin system with 14-variable CSS theming, media library polish (mode-button toggle states, locked column widths, repeat/shuffle text labels), visualizer width stability across player states, and CI pipelines that produce both a Linux Flatpak and a macOS DMG from every commit to main.

GTK4 is now the default interface (launch with sparkamp); TUI is available via sparkamp --tui. Adds media library with background scanning, spectrum visualizer with configurable color zones and mirror mode, bar visualizer improvements, shuffle persistence, and numerous GTK fixes including jump-window search, scroll-to-row, and replace-mode autoplay.
Initial public release featuring GStreamer audio backend, GTK4 GUI, TUI mode, 10-band EQ with pre-amp, media library, visualizer plugins, and CSS skinning.
